text:
mia: Kicking off Lacerta14b (int4) canary. Seeing memory spikes and occasional OOMs on long-context QA prompts. Canary config: batch=8, max_new_tokens=256, prefetch=on. Starting perf run now.

alex: Can you paste the perf snapshot / OOM stack? Also which quant backend (q4/q5) did we use?

mia: We used q4_k_m (the new pack). Paste snapshot: 
```
--- perf snapshot ---
workload: 1k short answers + 200 long-form
batch=8, max_new_tokens=256
P50 latency: 120ms
P95 latency: 430ms
tokens/sec: 78
GPU mem per worker: 32.6 GiB (peak)
OOM log: AssertionError: allocation failed at kv_cache_alloc()
node: gw-ml-14-02
stack: serving_runtime::kv::alloc -> kv_cache::reserve -> cudaMalloc -> OOM
--- end ---
```

ryan: hmm looks like KV cache blow-up on some long contexts. Two quick levers: reduce batch (to 4) or lower max_new_tokens default to 128 for canary. Also try soft-evict: `kv_trim_threshold=0.75` + `kv_cushion=0.12` and turn `prefetch=false` for this model.

mia: I tried batch=4 and prefetch=false locally — OOMs disappeared but p95 jumped to ~560ms and throughput dropped ~35%. Quality didn't change much on the short QA eval. Long-form latency increased a lot.

alex: For rollback/fallback strategy, propose: 1) per-request gating: if estimated response tokens > 200 -> route to Lacerta13b-int8 variant; 2) keep Lacerta14b as default for <=200 tokens. We can implement a policy in router easily.

mia: Good call. For the canary we also need a quick patch to avoid unbounded KV growth: enable `max_kv_size=48M` and `evict_policy=LRU_soft`. That should cap memory worst-case.

ryan: Also run a micro-benchmark comparing quality between Lacerta14b-int4 and Lacerta13b-int8 on our eval set (1000 prompts). Measure BLEU/ROUGE/QA-F1 and a simple hallucination check. If quality delta > 1.5% on QA-F1 we keep routing but mark as degraded in console.

mia: Planning to run bench now. Prompt sets: short-answer (1k), summarization (200), long-dialogue (100). Will push results in ~30m.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of lacerta14b-int4 to prod pool "canary-ml" started (10% nodes). Rollout id: r-20260323-01.

alex: One more ops tweak — on kernel selection side, try `max_prefetch_read=4` (instead of default 8) and enable `kv_slot_compact=true` on the canary. Those reduce concurrent device allocations.

mia: Copy. I'll run three variants: (A) batch=4, max_new=256, prefetch=false, kv_trim=0.75; (B) batch=6, max_new=128, prefetch=true, kv_cushion=0.12; (C) batch=8, max_new=128 + max_kv_size cap. Will report latency + OOM events + quality diffs.

ryan: If C looks stable, we can try soft rollout with 25% traffic and strict SLO gate (p95 < 500ms, OOM rate < 0.1%). Otherwise fallback policy to Lacerta13b-int8 as alex suggested.

mia: Running now, will post logs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
